# Ragdoll Mail

> Free, open-source mail app for Mac and Windows with a command line built in, so AI agents (Claude Code, Codex and any agent that runs shell commands) can search the mailbox and write replies; the person approves every send. Search runs on a local SQLite full-text index. Works with any IMAP mailbox, including Gmail, iCloud, Fastmail, Tencent Exmail (腾讯企业邮箱), QQ Mail and 163.

- For AI agents: the `ragdoll` command (install it from the app: Settings → Command line). `search`, `thread`, `read`, `draft --reply`, `check`, `open` and `send`, each with `--json`. Drafts are saved in the mailbox's real Drafts folder and open in the app. `send` needs an explicit yes, and a draft is never sent twice. No API key, no OAuth app, no usage quota: plain IMAP and SMTP to the user's own server.
- Why it exists: AI mail apps are mostly paid and limited to Gmail or Outlook; free command-line mail tools such as Himalaya send each search to the mail server. Measured on a Tencent Exmail inbox of 5,044 mails: one command-line search on the server took about 1 s (0.9 s to sign in, 0.13 s to search) and returned the whole folder for any word; Ragdoll Mail's local index answered in 6 ms with the 989 matching mails.
- Price: free, MIT license, no ads, no account, no server of ours.
- Platforms: macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows 10/11. No phone app. One mailbox per window.
- Safety: up to 30 s to undo a send; warns when the text says "attached" and nothing is attached, the subject is empty, or a placeholder such as [Name] is left. Send later.
- Reading: whole conversations, attachments (drag them to the desktop on a Mac), meeting invitations shown as a card with Add to Calendar, and a one-click Unsubscribe for newsletters (List-Unsubscribe, RFC 8058).
- Setup: type the address and password. For a company domain the app reads the domain's MX records and fills in the servers for Tencent Exmail, Google Workspace, Alibaba Mail, NetEase enterprise mail, iCloud, Fastmail, Zoho and Yandex.
- Password: kept in macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager. Many mailboxes need an app password (Exmail: 客户端专用密码; QQ Mail and 163: 授权码).
